identity: (net_id, native logical load pin, physical BEL pin) maps through existing used site routing to a physical SitePinInst and frozen ConnectionTask ID, or to a proven internal source driver.
exported_evidence: Complete selected-net site pin identities and native node representatives
All labelled wires and their BEL pins for selected net/site pairs
invariants: No new route is chosen and no DCP is written.
Every mapped input matches the exact footprint task pin and native PIP writeback preparation.
Each traversed site wire has one driver and each mux output has one enabled site PIP.
Unselected muxes, cycles, wrong net labels, ambiguous drivers and unsupported route-throughs are rejected.
A site-local load and the net source output site pin must reach the same functional BEL driver.
SDK and independent exported-connectivity results agree.
Every selected physical task has native logical-load delay coverage.
cardinality: Multiple logical loads may share a physical task; a site-local load has no intersite routing task. Keep each logical load independently; do not average their delays.

observation_units.path_depth: directed PIP count, not physical wirelength

min_max_semantics: Net-delay corner observations include site portions. Full-path slack depends additionally on clock paths, other cells/nets and timing constraints. Neither is a static additive PIP weight.
no_reported_path: Missing native path queries remain explicit; they are not zero slack, a timing pass, or a demonstrated reason for absence.
reported_unconstrained_path: An object exists but SLACK, REQUIREMENT and REQUIRED_TIME are empty and the detailed native report states Slack: inf. Preserve the path but do not assign a finite slack or count a timing pass.
